item.title: DeepSeek Founder Proposes AI Training Method to Bypass GPU Limits
item.description: A new artificial intelligence (AI) model training technique, co-authored by DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng and Peking University researchers, aims to bypass graphics processing unit (GPU) memory constraints. This development underscores the Hangzhou start-up’s focus on maximising cost efficiency amid a computational power deficit compared to US industry leaders.

item.title: Solo Living Safety App Goes Viral, Rebrands as Demumu for Global Users
item.description: An app named "Are you dead?" has garnered significant attention in China, experiencing a surge in downloads and widespread social media discussion. Designed as a "lightweight safety tool" for people living alone, the organisation has introduced a subscription fee and changed its name for a global audience.

item.title: Zhipu AI Advances China's Chip Independence With Huawei-Trained Model
item.description: Chinese artificial intelligence firm Zhipu AI announced its new image generation model was trained on chips from Huawei Technologies, making it the first powerful open-source model developed on an entirely domestic training stack, marking a significant step towards domestic technology independence. This development demonstrates the feasibility of creating powerful multimodal models without relying on United States semiconductors.

item.title: Meta Closes VR Gaming Studios, Shifts Focus to AR Glasses
item.description: Meta's Reality Labs is reportedly laying off up to 10% of its staff, leading to the closure of several internal studios that developed games for Meta Quest. These studio closures include Armature, Twisted Pixel, and Sanzaru Games. Credit: META Armature was responsible for the virtual reality (VR) port of Resident Evil 4. item.title: Australia's Social Media Ban Deactivates Millions of Teen Accounts
item.description: Australia's new social media ban for under-16s has led to the deactivation of approximately 4.7 million teen accounts within its first month, according to the country's internet regulator. This swift impact signals the measure's effectiveness.

item.title: Spotify Increases Premium Subscription Price
item.description: Spotify is set to raise the monthly price of its premium subscription plan by USD 1 to USD 12.99. This adjustment will affect users in the United States, Estonia, and Latvia.

item.title: Wikipedia Marks 25 Years, Establishes Major AI Partnerships
item.description: Wikipedia has marked its 25th anniversary by announcing partnerships with several major artificial intelligence companies. This initiative aims to integrate the platform's extensive human-governed knowledge into AI systems at scale.

item.title: Uber WeChat Partnership Drives Chinese Tourist Demand
item.description: Uber Technologies' strategic partnership with Tencent Holdings' super app WeChat is yielding significant dividends. The ride-hailing operator is meeting a critical demand from Chinese travellers overseas.

item.title: OpenAI to Introduce Advertisements in ChatGPT to Boost Revenue
item.description: OpenAI will begin testing advertisements with select US ChatGPT users, aiming to boost revenue and finance the high development costs of its artificial intelligence technology. Credit: OpenAI These ads will be tested with users on the free tier and the globally expanding Go plan, appearing in the coming weeks. They will remain separate from answers generated by ChatGPT. item.title: iPhone Displays May Diverge, Pro Models Hint at Under-Display Area
item.description: A recent leak indicates future iPhone models will present strikingly different display designs depending on the model, while some next-generation iPhones are anticipated to launch in Sept. This report details specifications for four devices: iPhone 18, second-generation iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone 18 Pro Max.
